rv.q: The clever direction and choreography of Kevin P. Hill, NSMT’s producing artistic director, quickly mitigates the impact of these necessary modifications and the blending of the several stories the show tells begins to unfold in the hands of a versatile 12-person cast, each of whom nimbly plays more than one role.
This is without a doubt musical storytelling at its best.

Twenty-five years after the events that inspired it, the show finds its power not in diminishing the horror of that day, but in focusing on what ordinary people chose to do in its immediate aftermath.

Come from Away is not without moments of shock, distress and uncertainty, but holds many more moments of warmth, encouragement and humor delivered in rich harmony that could very well spark a renewed faith in humanity.
Lively choreography and crisp direction (both by Kevin P. Hill) and snappy lyrics and dialogue combine to create a show well worth traveling to the North Shore to see.
